BiblicalUsage: The roar in this word belongs to lions, and to men who act like them. Isaiah hears an invading army whose roaring shall be like a lion, laying hold of the prey with none to deliver it, and Zechariah hears the roaring of young lions over the spoiled pride of Jordan. Job answers that the roaring of the lion and the teeth of the young lions are broken, and Ezekiel hears the same noise over desolate palaces and wasted cities.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the roar is the sound of power, and Scripture keeps showing that power broken. The lion roars, the teeth are broken, and the Lord who hears the roar is the one who ends it.
